notes: Deck for TruthNet v0.4.0 (D-SITE-091..095). Acts: 1 = provenance warm-up (KS1), 2 = framing/context (KS2), 3 = feeling/system (KS3). truth takes three values: fake | real | unsure. 'unsure' marks a genuinely undecidable card — checking turns up nothing either way, and CAN'T TELL is the rewarded answer. The flood card is NOT unsure: it is undecidable from pixels but decided by checking (verify load-bearing). v0.4 counterexamples break the style shortcut: loud-but-true (football, trip), calm-but-false (museum), honest ad (zapp), labelled AI used honestly (library). Base rate 11 fake / 8 real / 1 unsure, so blanket scepticism scores 55%, down from 71%. All Act 2/3 cards carry a verify block; tells are written in claim-and-evidence language, never 'quiet means true'. Outrage/scapegoat/urgency cards use fictional targets only — never a real school, place, group or person. Act 3 keeps the giveaway late so the sting (anchored to it) lands on its card. measure = the C1 instrument, v2: 3 pre + 3 post novel items (loud-true, quiet-false, loud-fake in each set) so a style-matcher scores 1/3, not full marks; measurement cards now CARRY verify blocks — checking is allowed and silently counted, but there are no reveals and no tokens (D-SITE-092 amended by D-SITE-095).

cards.question: Real photo, or made by a computer?
cards.tellOk: Count the legs — there are more than four. And the grass melts into mush at the edges. No real dog looks like this; a computer drew it.
cards.tellNo: Count the legs — more than four. The grass melts into mush around the paws too. Clues like these give this one away — though good fakes won't always be this careless.

cards.tellNo: This one's real — four legs, natural fur, nothing melting or scrambled. Careful though: fakes get better every year, so spotting glitches won't always save you. The later tricks will.

cards.tellNo: Tricky — the photo is completely real. But it's nine years old, and 'HAPPENING NOW' was bolted on today. You can't see that in the pixels — only a source check shows it. An old truth, re-posted as new, is a lie.

cards.tellNo: Check the maths: '9 out of 10 can't' means 10% can — so where did 'the 1%' come from? Nobody counted anything. Made-up numbers dressed as facts are a tactic: they sound precise, so you don't check.

cards.cap: This school just BANNED break time 😡 SHARE if you think this is WRONG
cards.question: Is the ANGER earned?
cards.tellOk: Anger is the product. No school is named, no rule is shown — just an empty playground and 'SHARE if you're angry'. Rage makes you share before you think, and shares are the payout.
cards.tellNo: Count the facts: no school named, no letter, no rule — just a photo of an empty playground and an instruction to be angry. The story is a feeling with nothing under it. Manufactured outrage is a tactic: anger spreads faster than checking.

cards.tellNo: It looked like rage-bait — but the school's letter confirms it, and the coach company really shut. The anger is real AND the story is real. Loud feelings don't make a thing false; missing evidence does.

cards.cap: Our park was PERFECT until the new lot from Grimley Road moved in 😤 everything's worse now
cards.question: Who's really being blamed?
cards.tellOk: Look at the evidence: some litter. Look at the claim: a whole group of people ruined everything. Nothing connects them. Blaming a group for everything is a tactic with a name — scapegoating — and it works because anger feels like evidence.
cards.tellNo: The evidence is a messy bin. The claim is that a whole group ruined everything — with no proof, just 'them'. That tactic is called scapegoating: pick a group, pin every problem on them, and let anger do the thinking.

lines: 🗑️ Same litter problem for years
👤 Only ever posts about 'the new lot'
🤝 Grimley Road is never asked

cards.cap: FREE game credit codes 🎮 DELETING IN 1 HOUR ⏰ share with 3 friends to unlock
cards.question: Why the countdown?
cards.tellOk: The clock is the trick. 'One hour' exists to stop you thinking, and 'share with 3 friends' is the real goal — you're the advert. There are no codes.
cards.tellNo: Real giveaways don't need a panic timer. The countdown exists so you don't stop to check, and 'share with 3 friends' is the point — the post spreads itself through you. The codes never existed.

lines: ⏰ The '1 hour' post is 6 days old
🎮 The game says codes aren't given this way
🔁 Thousands shared and got nothing

cards.cap: AD | ZAPP sent me their new flavour to try. It's decent — bit sweet for me tbh. #ad #gifted
cards.question: He's being paid… so is it all fake?
cards.tellOk: Being paid doesn't make it a lie. He says AD up front and tells you what he didn't like. Honest ads exist — the tell isn't the money, it's whether they hide it.
cards.tellNo: Tempting to call paid = fake — but he told you it was an ad, and even said it was too sweet. The dishonest version hides the #ad and fakes the love. Declared and balanced is as honest as an advert gets.

lines: 🏷️ 'AD' declared right at the start
👎 He criticises the product — hidden ads never do
📜 His other sponsored posts are labelled too

cards.cap: Summer Reading Club starts Saturday! 🌳📚 (picture: AI illustration)
cards.question: Computer-made picture… honest post?
cards.tellOk: The picture IS computer-made — and the post says so. The reading club is real. AI isn't the lie; hiding it is. A labelled illustration is just a picture, like a drawing on a poster.
cards.tellNo: The image is AI — but they TOLD you, and the club is real. 'Computer-made' and 'dishonest' aren't the same thing. The question is never just how a picture was made; it's what the post claims — and this claim is true.

lines: 🖼️ Labelled 'AI illustration' — nothing hidden
📚 The club is on the library's own site
🏛️ A real library, posting for years

cards.cap: I gave a stranger £100,000 and changed his life forever ❤️
cards.question: Kindness, or content?
cards.tellOk: Follow the money. The £100,000 may be real — the kindness isn't the point of it. The stranger is a prop, the emotion is the product, and 8 million views is the payout. Ask who profits from you feeling this.
cards.tellNo: Don't judge the man — judge the system. The money may be real, but the giving isn't kindness, it's content. The person is a prop and the emotion is the product. The tell isn't in the picture; it's in who profits from you feeling this.

lines: 💰 Ads earn more than he gives away
🎬 A 12-person film crew in the credits
📈 The 'stranger' is in 3 other videos

cards.cap: Everyone's saying HALF the shops in Milbury are closing down 😳 look at this
cards.question: Can anyone actually tell from this?
cards.tellOk: Right call. The photo shows… a street with people on it. 'Everyone's saying' names nobody, and checking turns up nothing either way. When even checking settles nothing, 'can't tell yet' is the honest answer — and not worth sharing until someone can.
cards.tellNo: Trick question — nobody could tell. The photo's just a street; 'everyone' is no one; and checking finds nothing solid either way. Calling it REAL spreads a rumour; calling it FAKE is still a guess. CAN'T TELL was the smart move.

lines: 👤 'Everyone' = nobody named, ever
📰 No news story confirms it — none denies it
📸 The photo shows… a normal street
